column4: A mechanical 35 mm film camera fired close to the ear: the shutter's two crisp metallic clicks and a short rattle of the film winding on. Dry, close, outdoors at night, no music.
An old photographic flash unit charging up: a thin high electronic whine rising in pitch and then cutting off suddenly. Close, dry, no music.
A cheap 1990s compact camera's autofocus confirmation: two quick high electronic beeps from a tiny speaker. Close, dry, no music.
One heavy footstep landing on packed dirt outdoors at night, followed by the short creak of an old wooden board. Close, no music.
A 1990s belt pager receiving a message: two short shrill beeps from a tiny cheap speaker. Close, dry, no music.

An old AM transistor radio being tuned late at night: hiss and whistles settling onto a hollow carrier hum, then a small tinny music box plays a slow sad five note phrase, then plays the same phrase again. Lo-fi, mono, distant, no voices.

On an old AM transistor radio late at night a small tinny music box plays a slow sad five note phrase but stops one note short, then the station drifts away into hiss and tuning whistles. Lo-fi, mono, no voices.
One short radio time signal pip, a pure high beep a tenth of a second long, heard on an old AM transistor radio with faint hiss, then silence.

The steady unbroken dial tone of a 1990s Czech telephone exchange, a 425 hertz tone heard through an old telephone handset earpiece, with faint line hiss and a little hum, unchanging from start to end.
One short telephone keypad tone: the dual-frequency beep of pressing a single key on a 1990s push-button phone, heard through the handset earpiece, then silence.
Quiet telephone line noise heard in an old handset during a call: soft hiss, faint crackle and a low hum, steady, seamless loop, no tones, no voices.
The 'number not in service' signal of an old telephone line heard through a handset: three short rising electronic tones, then silence. Lo-fi, no voices.
The steady electrical buzz of an old neon sign's transformer at night: a 100 hertz hum with a slight crackle, close, seamless loop, no music.
A single small electric tick and fizz from an old neon tube flickering, close, quiet.
One tiny dry crackle from a neon sign tube, a short electric snap, close, quiet.
A faint electric click and buzz blip from an old neon tube, very short, close.
An old neon sign tube striking on: a sharp electric pop, then a swelling crackling buzz that settles into a steady hum, close, no music.
A failing neon sign tube sputtering on and off: irregular electric crackles and fizzing pops, close, no music.
A moth bumping softly against a glass light tube twice: two tiny light taps and a faint flutter of wings, very close, quiet.
The steady 1 kHz test tone from a small old black and white television's tinny speaker after the broadcast has closed down, with faint hiss, unchanging, seamless loop.
One single footstep in heavy work boots in fresh wet snow a few centimetres deep over grass, a soft squeaky crunch, outdoors, very close, nothing else. No music.
One single footstep in heavy work boots in fresh wet snow a few centimetres deep over grass, a soft squeaky crunch, outdoors, very close, nothing else. A little heavier. No music.
One single footstep in heavy work boots in fresh wet snow a few centimetres deep over grass, a soft squeaky crunch, outdoors, very close, nothing else. Slightly lighter, quicker. No music.
One single footstep in heavy work boots in fresh wet snow a few centimetres deep over grass, a soft squeaky crunch, outdoors, very close, nothing else. The other foot, a touch different. No music.
One single footstep in heavy work boots landing in a shallow rain puddle on a dirt path, a wet slap and a small splash, outdoors, very close, nothing else. No music.
One single footstep in heavy work boots landing in a shallow rain puddle on a dirt path, a wet slap and a small splash, outdoors, very close, nothing else. A little heavier. No music.
One single footstep in heavy work boots landing in a shallow rain puddle on a dirt path, a wet slap and a small splash, outdoors, very close, nothing else. Slightly lighter, quicker. No music.

One single footstep in heavy work boots landing in a shallow rain puddle on a dirt path, a wet slap and a small splash, outdoors, very close, nothing else. The other foot, a touch different. No music.

The metal clip of a flag rope blown by the wind against a hollow aluminium flagpole: two or three irregular clinks and a soft slap of the rope, outdoors, from a few metres away, nothing else. No music.
A gust slaps a flag rope against a hollow aluminium flagpole: a quick run of hollow metallic clinks, then quiet, outdoors, from a few metres away, nothing else. No music.

The steady electrical buzz of an old fluorescent tube in a small concrete washroom at night, with a faint irregular flicker tick now and then, heard from just outside its door, seamless loop. No music.
A dripping tap in an empty concrete washroom at night: slow single drops falling into a metal sink, a small hollow echo, seamless loop. No music.
Distant voices of a few adults talking and laughing around a campfire on the far side of a field at night, the words not understandable, faint, outdoors, crickets. No music.
Distant children shouting and laughing as they play on a meadow on a late summer afternoon, far away, the words not understandable, outdoors. No music.
A single farm dog barking a few times far away across fields at night, echoing a little, outdoors, nothing else. No music.
An old car passing on a country road some distance away at night, coming nearer and fading away, the hiss of its tyres, outdoors. No music.
A diesel train's horn far away across the countryside at night, two long notes, then the faint rumble of the train fading into the distance, outdoors. No music.
A small village church bell ringing slowly far away across the fields, heard faintly in the open air, outdoors. No music.
Steady rain drumming on the corrugated tin roof of a small shed, heard from just outside it a few metres away, the metallic patter and the water running off the eaves, seamless loop. No music.
Steady rain falling on the flat water of a small lake, a soft hiss of countless drops on water and a few bigger plops, heard from the shore, seamless loop. No music.
Rain falling on the leaves of birch and spruce trees overhead, a soft crackling patter and heavier drops falling from the branches, outdoors, seamless loop. No music.
The soft swish of the nylon sleeves of a work jacket brushing against the body with one walking step, very close, quiet, nothing else. No music.
The soft rustle of a nylon work jacket with one walking step, the other arm, very close, quiet, nothing else. No music.
A quick nylon jacket swish and rustle with one running stride, very close, nothing else. No music.
A bunch of keys on a ring hanging from a belt jingling with one running stride, a few light metallic clinks, very close, nothing else. No music.
A bunch of keys on a ring hanging from a belt jingling with one running stride, a slightly different jingle, very close, nothing else. No music.
The dry hinges of an old wooden cabin door creaking briefly as it swings open, heard from a few metres away outdoors, nothing else. No music.
A short squeak of rusty hinges as a light wooden door is pushed open, heard from a few metres away outdoors, nothing else. No music.
A wooden cabin door swinging shut against its frame: a soft hollow thud and the click of the latch, heard from a few metres away outdoors, nothing else. No music.
A light wooden door banging shut in its frame with a rattle of the latch, heard from a few metres away outdoors, nothing else. No music.
